scope: Continued referee revision: the unordered intrinsic block cover and all-rank scalar-gerbe period gcd(N,3) are proved on reduced Poisson strata. On full support N=3k, the coefficient space is affine, and a prescribed finite second jet lifts directly to a covariant even algebraic centre on a neighborhood of the entire h=0 section. One-block filtration proves regularity; the third Veronese and its global degree-one centre descend to the actual reduced Poisson stratum. Classical base dimension is 2k (4 for rank-four cubic fourfolds). General m>0,k>=2 remains open. Proof reading, exact computation, typesetting, visual inspection and persistence are distinct.

material_corrections: The relative forgetful scheme morphism is affine of finite type, not a closed immersion into the base.
Relative rank strata use the simultaneous scalar action (F,P)->(aF,a^-1 P) and reduced structures.
The threefold derived-recovery corollary explicitly assumes left/right noetherian ambient A over C; its central quotient B inherits noetherianity.
Ambient PBW alone does not imply S-freeness of the central quotient; regular highest active symbol is a sufficient condition, and A/(u^3) demonstrates the obstruction.

The semisimple kernel calculation is attributed precisely to Derdzinski--Gal Theorem B; radical elimination from smoothness remains a separate argument. Bondal section 4 supplies the earlier divergence-free homogeneous lift.

Pym arXiv v1 Theorem 1.3 / Proposition 5.7 are contradicted by the proved split cubic fourfold example. The disconnected-centre failure of Lemma 5.5 is exhibited explicitly; no assertion is made about an unverified published or corrected text.
The divided-commutator kernel commutes with arbitrary base change on the constant-rank open, whereas the ordinary centre can enlarge at h-torsion or at h=0.
Two normalized central lifts have transition Omega_j=a_ij Omega_i+c_ij; equality of their classical limits does not force a_ij=1 or equality of their central ideals.
The fixed-coordinate coefficient-family existence theorem does not assert a coefficient-independent parameter open or equivariant descent to the full Poisson moduli stack.

Uncorrected scalar-weight equivariance gives a gerbe family. When gcd(m,3)=1, the character theta=(det N)^r lambda^s with mr-3s=1 removes degree weights, giving actual graded-algebra descent to the stated reduced Poisson stratum open.
The abstract, introduction and ambient-recovery discussion distinguish the 17-dimensional reduced Poisson base from the unproved dimension of the fixed-nonzero-h noncommutative moduli image.

Full-G equivariance generally requires dropping the pure-central-coefficient gauge. All-support existence includes every ternary restriction type near h=0, with the universal second jet. Standard zero-restriction matching is obstructed for N>=6; other stratumwise comparisons and multiple-block changes remain separate.

Pointwise existence of a non-scalar central element is explicitly credited to Etingof--Ginzburg. Mixed quadratic coefficients by themselves are not claimed as new: for invertible Hesse t they can be translated to the existing presentation.

The general lifting obstruction is independent of any literature-error claim and is C^{pi_0(C)}/C; connectedness gives vanishing, while disconnectedness alone does not assert that every section has a nonzero obstruction.
The ambient recovery appendix uses A for the ambient algebra and B for its central quotient, consistently with the quantization part.
The cubic-fourfold Hessian plane lies in ambient P^5, not in X. Hessian reducibility by itself does not imply a rank-four Poisson structure, as shown by the smooth (1,1,4) example.
For every r>=2 the lifting obstruction has the component-constant description only at the defining degree d; for another twist e the relevant group is H^1(I_C^(r-1)(e-d)).

In the original degree-one grading, the descended centre is a cubic line subbundle and its homogeneous ideal, without a chosen global generator. In the lambda-twisted third Veronese the central element has weight zero and does descend as a global degree-one generator.

Tor in the central-linear-extension display uses the right/left module convention. The u variables form a regular sequence in ambient A, not necessarily in its quotient B; on zero restriction Omega mod(u)=0.

The singular-point line uses pullback M^-1, hence scalar weight -1; tensoring degree d with its d-th power removes the algebra weight d. This uses an equivariant line over each stratum, not a character splitting of the constant group. No congruence condition on m is needed on these two strata.

EG Proposition 8.1.1(i), published pp.1407-1408, already supplies a formal centre with prescribed classical residue and does not assume isolated singularities. Its relative and reductive-compatible formal argument is credited; none of those general facts is claimed as new.

Finite completion Khat/h^ell Khat=K/h^ell K algebraizes a prescribed finite jet; choosing ell=3 preserves the universal Hessian second jet. It does not identify an arbitrary whole formal series with a rational expression.
The global centering obstruction permits dependence on every coefficient of the smooth full cubic, nonzero eta and h; it does not contradict the direct full-support central-kernel construction.

For N>=6, any global even centre cannot match the standard zero-restriction central line on the whole zero stratum, already formally. In the original grading the descended centre is a line; in the lambda-twisted third Veronese it has an actual global degree-one generator. No extension over all h or quotient nonisomorphism is concluded.

The scalar gerbe has exact order gcd(N,3), so for 3|N the obstruction is to every weight-one invertible sheaf, not only to characters. The rank-two family has lambda-twisted third-Veronese descent for every N; the new full-support family also has this descent. No nonexistence of other ambient or Morita models is asserted.

The third Veronese retains degreewise local freeness and a regular degree-one centre, but AS-regularity is not transferred to it. Its fibre polarization is O(3); fibrewise qgr equivalence is stated with noetherian hypotheses and is not a claim of global relative category descent.

Block pointwise intrinsicness is already in the manuscript normal form discussion; the new finite-etale cover is its family form. The incidence is the reduced rank stratum, not an unproved scheme-theoretic identification of the unreduced Jacobi equations.

Full-support affineness permits direct lifting of a finite jet, without formal completion. The tensor product is not assumed to be a domain: a single-block degree filtration proves central regularity.

The gerbe period gcd(N,3) is now proved on every entire nonzero rank stratum. This does not assert the same period on every dense open or its generic point. The positive simultaneous-selection theorem covers m=0 and earlier k=1; m>0,k>=2 remains open.
Full-support base dimension 2k, including dimension4 for rank-four cubic fourfolds, is not a claim about the image of abstract noncommutative algebra isomorphism classes at fixed nonzero h.

Two monic Diamond systems and overlaps; six universal central commutators; h=0 limits; potential syzygies; denominator scopes; two negative controls; 17-term Fermat certificate. Recalculated result exactly matches the saved JSON without --write.

Exact identity over the rational function field with independent Hesse and mixed coefficients: the translated cubic including its constant term and all three free-word quadratic relations agree with the stated Etingof--Ginzburg presentation. This does not prove centrality or PBW flatness.

The idempotent ranks over C are 0,1,2,4,5,6. Smoothness, the coordinate-invariant projection implication and the Poisson classification are proved in the manuscript, not by this finite computation.

No specialization, parameter inversion or truncation. General linear/scalar covariance, smoothness, AS conditions and stack descent are not computationally checked here.

The tangent conic-line equivariant-left-inverse system has coefficient/augmented ranks 18/19, independently 4/5 after torus restriction. Exact Groebner reductions put a positive power of each variable in both example gradient ideals. Full stabilizer classification, orbit regularity, quantum centrality and moduli descent are mathematical proofs outside this computation.

Exact QQ/Laurent identities for the known general CMR nodal formula: decreasing monic rewrite rules, only critical overlap zyx, all three central commutators, symmetric-Jacobian parameter map, regular polynomial normalization at t=0, prescribed classical residue, scalar/mu3 weights, corrected node-swap covariance and alternative centering. No PBW or flatness at t=+/-2, full stabilizer classification, global support equivariance or moduli descent is certified by this finite computation.

Six exact smooth translated-Hesse examples (n,k,m)=(3,1,2),(4,2,0),(6,2,2),(7,3,0),(10,3,3),(10,4,0): all Jacobi triples and Casimir equations, vanishing cross-block Hessians and the intrinsic Hessian contraction sum lambda_s^2 det(Hess_s), with independent Poisson parameters. This does not prove the general normal form, full-support affine lifting, quantum centrality, gerbe period or stack descent.

remaining_limits: The Pym comparison is restricted to checked arXiv:1507.05668v1. Published metadata, the accepted-manuscript repository record and ordinary public access routes were checked, but published/accepted full text was not obtained; no claim is made about an unverified correction or its absence.

Brueckmann original proofs (1976 Satz 3 / 1977 Satz 6) were not obtained; Fu--Hwang Lemma 4.1 and its attribution were verified. The needed low-twist vanishing is proved self-containedly in the manuscript, so these unavailable proofs are no longer a mathematical dependency of that criterion.

Comprehensive novelty of the normal form, component theorem, algebraic prescribed-jet selections and obstructions is not established. Formal centres, BWB, affine reductive quotients, averaging, Picard/gerbe principles, completion, Veronese equivalence and line twists are credited as known inputs.

The rank-two and full-support simultaneous-selection theorems exclude zero Poisson P=0 and apply to a neighborhood of the entire deformation zero section, not the entire h line. The full-support case directly lifts a finite jet and does not require algebraizing an arbitrary whole formal series.

For N>=6 the standard sym(F) line on the whole zero-restriction stratum cannot be matched by any global even central line in the fixed ambient family. This does not prove abstract quotient nonisomorphism, qgr inequivalence or failure on every individual point; node/cusp formula comparison remains separate.

On every entire nonzero reduced rank stratum the scalar gerbe has period gcd(N,3); for 3|N no weight +/-1 line exists on a neighborhood containing the whole zero section. This is not a claim about every dense open or generic point. Third-Veronese descent is constructed for the rank-two and full-support centre families; other ambient or Morita models and categories are not ruled out.

AS-regularity is not asserted for Veronese algebras. The cited fibrewise qgr equivalence assumes left/right noetherianity and is distinct from a global relative category equivalence or smoothness at every closed parameter.

Simultaneous centre selection on m>0,k>=2 remains open. The known pointwise/fixed-block quantization and the new full-support family do not solve that case. Dimensions17 for cubic-threefold rank2 and4 for cubic-fourfold rank4 describe the reduced Poisson-pair bases, not fixed-nonzero-h images in abstract noncommutative moduli.

Only the six-example general-dimension multiblock verifier was executed for A-v61; fourteen earlier computations are retained with matching hashes. Mathematical reading and exact coefficient identities are not formal proof-assistant verification or referee acceptance.
